newsitem.title: USA: Judge puts off decision on Marvel for now.
newsitem.headline: Judge puts off decision on Marvel for now.

text.p: Judge has issued a temporary stay that maintains the status quo in the battle between Marvel Holdings Inc's bondholders and Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's banks.

Judge Roderick McKelvie of the U.S. District Court in Delaware said he would have a hearing next Tuesday at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT to decide whether he has the jurisdiction to issue a restraining order against the bondholders replacing the board of Marvel Entertainment.
Marvel Holdings with the approval of the banks had requested the stay until a June 19 hearing on the merits of this issue.

Attorney for the banks, Douglas Leibhafsky, told McKelvie that "Marvel Entertainment is inslovent . . . (without a stay) Mr. Ichan and his friends will take over our assets. We are owed $710 million. The lunatics will be running the asylum."
Leibhafsky said that Blackstone Investments is putting together a due diligence report and the results are to be released June 1.
Earlier Wednesday, a Marvel spokesman told Reuters that Marvel believes an auction would be in the best interest of the creditors and the debtor.
But bondholder attorney, David Friedman, told McKelvie "when a bank wants to liquidate the assets of a company, it's because they're going to be paid off in full" and bondholders will get nothing.
"If the company is liquidated . . . we're going to be irrepairably harmed."
